data.name: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC)
data.description: Cancer of the kidney; target indication for everolimus treatment in clinical practice.
data.description_beginner: The most common form of kidney cancer. It's an approved use for the mTOR-blocking drug everolimus in clinical practice.

evidence.label: Human study

studies.finding: Everolimus extended median progression-free survival from 1.9 to 4.0 months versus placebo in metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

studies.title: Temsirolimus, interferon alfa, or both for advanced renal-cell carcinoma
studies.authors: Hudes G; Carducci M; Tomczak P; Dutcher J; Figlin R; Kapoor A; Staroslawska E; Sosman J; McDermott D; Bodrogi I; Kovacevic Z; Lesovoy V; Schmidt-Wolf IG; Barbarash O; Gokmen E; O'Toole T; Lustgarten S; Moore L; Motzer RJ

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Temsirolimus alone extended median overall survival to 10.9 months versus 7.3 months with interferon alfa in poor-prognosis metastatic kidney cancer; rash, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia were more common with temsirolimus.

studies.title: Circadian regulation of mTOR by the ubiquitin pathway in renal cell carcinoma
studies.authors: Okazaki H; Matsunaga N; Fujioka T; Okazaki F; Akagawa Y; Tsurudome Y; Ono M; Kuwano M; Koyanagi S; Ohdo S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In mouse kidney tumours, active phosphorylated mTOR and total mTOR protein followed a 24-hour rhythm, set by the clock through the ubiquitin ligase Fbxw7. Giving everolimus when mTOR was high improved survival compared with other dosing times. Same drug, same dose - the clock time of dosing changed the outcome.

studies.title: SPOP-mediated ZMYND8 ubiquitination and phase separation exclusion drives mTOR inhibitor resistance in kidney cancer
studies.authors: Tang B; Sun R; Shao J; Wu QY; Yan Y; Wang D; Yu Z; Hu L; Chen Y; Liao C; Wei Q; Bao Y; Huang H

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: ccRCC cell lines (in vitro); mouse xenograft tumors treated with a NEK7-targeting PROTAC
studies.finding: Identifies a mechanism of mTOR-inhibitor (everolimus/temsirolimus) resistance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: SPOP-driven K63-linked ubiquitination of ZMYND8 excludes it from phase-separation compartments, enabling a ZMYND8-ZHX2 complex that drives NEK7 transcription and alternative p70S6K activation independent of mTOR inhibition. A NEK7-targeting PROTAC restored everolimus sensitivity in ccRCC cells and mouse tumors, nominating NEK7 as a target to overcome mTOR-inhibitor resistance.

relations.mechanism: RECORD-1: everolimus roughly doubled progression-free survival after other targeted therapy failed.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In a clinical trial, everolimus roughly doubled the time before advanced kidney cancer got worse, after other treatments had stopped working.
relations.boundary: Second-line setting, after VEGF-targeted therapy - not first-line.

relations.mechanism: Renal cancers frequently carry lesions that leave mTORC1 constitutively active, which is why this tissue responds to mTOR inhibitors. In two phase III trials in metastatic RCC, temsirolimus extended overall survival versus interferon alfa in poor-prognosis patients (HUD2007), and everolimus extended progression-free survival versus placebo after VEGF-targeted therapy (MOT2008). That the tumour responds to the drug is not the same as mTORC1 initiating the cancer.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Many kidney cancers carry changes that leave mTORC1 stuck "on", which is why this cancer responds to mTOR-blocking drugs at all. In one large trial, people with advanced kidney cancer lived longer on temsirolimus; in another, everolimus slowed the cancer's growth for a few months. Responding to the drug is not proof that mTORC1 started the cancer.
relations.boundary: Correlative, plus two randomised human trials showing the tumour responds to mTOR inhibitors: overall survival in poor-prognosis first-line RCC with temsirolimus (HUD2007), progression-free survival only after VEGF-targeted therapy with everolimus (MOT2008). This is response to treatment, not a demonstration that mTORC1 activation initiates RCC. The bladder-cancer responder case IYE2012 was removed from this edge on 2026-10-09 as a citation-population mismatch (it describes bladder, not kidney).
relations.note: Replaces TUMOR-RCC, which asserted 'Tumor growth activates RCC' - a category error, since RCC is an instance of tumour growth, not a downstream target. 2026-10-09: IYE2012 (metastatic bladder cancer) removed as a supporting study and from the mechanism text; it was a citation-population mismatch. Human relevance now rests on the two RCC phase III trials MOT2008 and HUD2007. 2026-10-09 (later): corrected 'both trials extended survival' - only HUD2007 showed overall survival; MOT2008 (RECORD-1) showed progression-free survival.

relations.mechanism: In poor-prognosis renal cancer, temsirolimus improved overall survival against interferon - the hardest endpoint there is.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In hard-to-treat kidney cancer, temsirolimus helped patients live longer compared with an older drug.
relations.boundary: Poor-prognosis patients specifically; the combination arm did not beat temsirolimus alone.
relations.note: Overall survival, not a surrogate. Worth pointing at.
